items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1961-01-19
items.q: ...well, people like Lizzie Miles would sing...

ctx.x: It's a big difference from now to today. Them different dances, what they had today... I'm gonna put it on this here, a guitar, wow. Sure, sure, put it on. And, uh, you see the dances, them did, uh... Everybody was dipping... ...of where dancing... ...but they never had nobody throwing one another over one another's backs. They used to take in dance... ...and every one of them coming there, they had to be women... ...or they had to be men. ...but they couldn't get in, in the dances. Women, it's women. Now they're…

I remember that over here at Economy Hall... Economy Hall... ...and they'd give these concerts on Sunday night or so, I remember... ...toke... ...well, people like Lizzie Miles would sing... Well, Liz would sing... ...and Wilhelmina Barth used to play... ...and Bunk says he used to play... ...were those sort of like dances, or were they really a concert? It is a concert. It's a concert. You know, some cities will have a law against giving a dance on a Sunday night, so they'll call them concerts, but it'll be the…

It was only a majority of the time at the Economy Hall, it was on a Sunday night. Was it a real concert band or not? Sometime we gave a concert on a Sunday night. Mr. Toko, he used to run in concert because he used to have them cheering... ...and old folks to act. They used to have a stage in front, downstairs in the back, and they'd put a... ...a false stage up. Yeah. With what they call them, horses? Yeah, on those trestles and then a platform up on there. Well, they'd put a...make a stand, stand on there.…
